findings.title: ClaudeSessionScanner.estimate fuses dir-walk, memo, aggregation and note-priority logic in one untested orchestrator
findings.evidence: swiftlint (only_rules cyclomatic_complexity, function_body_length, nesting, type_body_length, large_tuple, closure_body_length; no .swiftlint.yml in repo so SwiftLint defaults used: cyclomatic warning 10 / error 20, function_body_length warning 50 / error 100) run via swiftlint lint --reporter json --config <scratch>/sl.yml Sources: function_body_length ERROR 107 lines (ceiling 100) at line 19; cyclomatic_complexity WARNING 17. Reading the body: it interleaves a FileManager directory walk, memo cache-hit replay, per-file scan dispatch, and a multi-branch if/else-if chain building the user-facing note string (lines ~118-140) from filesScanned / unpriced-model state; only the extracted internal scan(data:) function is unit-tested per its own doc comment.
findings.impact: The only untested surface of a cost scanner is exactly the part that decides which explanatory note the user sees and merges memo-hit numbers into the running total; a reordering of the if/else-if chain or an off-by-one in the memo merge would silently change what is shown with no red test to catch it.
findings.fix: Extract note-selection into a pure static func note(filesScanned:unpricedToday:unpricedLast7:) returning String?, and give it a table-driven characterization test covering all branches; keep estimate as a thin I/O shell calling scan plus note.
findings.cetico_evidence: The premise 'untested orchestrator' is false. estimate(projectsDir:) is tested end to end on its note branches: missing dir (ClaudeSessionScannerTests.swift:142-149), empty dir (:151-160), unpriced-model note (:230-246). Leftover function length is style (swiftlint could not be reproduced: sourcekitd missing).

findings.title: CodexSessionScanner.estimateDetailed repeats the same walk, memo and note-priority fusion as ClaudeSessionScanner
findings.evidence: swiftlint (same config and ceilings as above): function_body_length ERROR 105 lines (ceiling 100) at line 66; cyclomatic_complexity WARNING 16. The note chain here has 4 branches (filesScanned==0 / unpriced-not-empty / lossNote / default, lines ~163-176) and returns a sawUsage tuple consumed by CodexCost fallback selection logic, per the doc comment on this function.
findings.impact: Higher stakes than the Claude version: the doc comment explains sawUsage exists to avoid CodexCost silently handing display to a dead sqlite scanner, and that dependency lives inside the same 105-line I/O function with no isolated test of the note / sawUsage branch order.
findings.fix: Split into scanAndAggregate (walk, memo, I/O) and a pure noteAndSawUsage(...) helper; add a characterization test enumerating the 4 note branches plus the sawUsage / unpriced interaction the doc comment describes.
findings.cetico_evidence: The premise 'no isolated test of note/sawUsage' is false. CodexSessionScannerTests.swift:413-466 cover the missing/empty/different-note/unpriced-note branches, and CodexCostTests (:488-551) pin the sawUsage selection: session wins, never summed, unpriced sessions beat sqlite. Only the length remains, which is style.

findings.title: AnalyticsStore cost-merge closure nests loop, if/else-if, inner loop, switch and if/else-if with 4x duplicated existing-or-priced-or-zero logic
findings.evidence: swiftlint (same config): cyclomatic_complexity ERROR 26 (ceiling-error 20) and function_body_length ERROR 134 lines at line 81 (the estimatesProvider closure passed to init(usageStore:costEstimator:)); closure_body_length ERROR 103 lines at line 83. Reading it: for each opencode vendor it computes computedToday and computedLast7 via an almost-identical existingCost-greater-than-zero-else-priced-else-zero block repeated twice, then a create-or-merge branch, then a second for-loop over usageStore.vendors with a switch on openrouter/xai cases each doing its own existing-or-default merge - 4 structurally similar merge blocks, 3-4 levels of nesting.
findings.impact: This closure is the single place reconciling CostEstimator per-vendor totals with UsageStore live snapshot totals. With 4 near-duplicate merge blocks and no unit test isolating just the merge (it is a weak-capturing closure built at init time), a fix applied to one block is easy to forget in the other three - the shotgun-surgery risk this project own CLAUDE.md already warns about for cost scanners.
findings.fix: Factor the repeated existingCost-else-priced-else-zero rule into a small pure helper mergedCost(existing:usage:pricing:) returning Double, used by both today and last7 branches, and extract the closure body into a standalone internal static AnalyticsStore.mergeEstimates(costEstimator:usageStore:) that a test can call directly.
findings.cetico_evidence: AnalyticsStore.swift:83-196: the default estimatesProvider closure nests loops, if/else and switch, and repeats the existing-or-default merge (opencode today/last7, openrouter, xai). Tests always inject their own estimatesProvider (AnalyticsStoreTests.swift:31,58), so the real merge is never exercised. Refactor/test debt, no bug shown.

findings.title: VendorSectionView.extras(for:) switch measures over the cyclomatic ceiling but is a plain per-vendor dispatch, not tangled logic - real gap is duplicated openrouter/zai blocks with no test
findings.category: cyclomatic false-positive on dispatch plus untested duplication
findings.evidence: swiftlint (same config): cyclomatic_complexity ERROR 22 (ceiling-error 20) and function_body_length ERROR 160 lines (ceiling 100) at line 575. Reading the body: it is a switch over snap across the 9 VendorSnapshot cases with no nested branching inside most arms - the openrouter and zai cases (lines ~586-625) contain byte-for-byte identical roughly 30-line VStack/HStack blocks. Per this lens own false-positive rule, a flat switch over an enum reads as cognitively cheap even at a high cyclomatic count.
findings.impact: The number itself is not evidence of a hidden bug (confirmed by reading), but the duplicated openrouter/zai block is a latent-divergence risk: a future formatting fix applied to one arm and not the other silently ships inconsistent UI, and as a SwiftUI ViewBuilder body it has zero unit-test coverage by construction. Overlaps with a god-view finding already flagged on this file; flagging only the duplication plus testability angle here.
findings.fix: Extract the shared openrouter/zai top-models block into a single TopModelsList(models:) view, which alone drops the switch well below the body-length ceiling.
findings.cetico_evidence: VendorSectionView.swift:587-615 (openrouter) and :616-645 (zai) are identical top-models blocks.

findings.title: SettingsViewModel.diff 47-branch cyclomatic score is a tabular field-comparator, not tangled logic - real risk is the unenforced diff-every-field exhaustiveness contract
findings.category: cyclomatic false-positive on flat comparator plus missing exhaustiveness test
findings.evidence: swiftlint (same config): cyclomatic_complexity ERROR 47 (ceiling-error 20, more than 2x) and function_body_length ERROR 163 lines (ceiling 100) at line 107, static func diff(from:to:) returning [ConfigChange]. Reading the body: it is roughly 45 independent, unnested if old.X != new.X blocks appending a ConfigChange, across 12 TOML sections - no branch depends on another, so cognitive load is low despite the cyclomatic score, matching the lens documented false-positive pattern for tabular functions.
findings.impact: The function own doc comment states the real risk directly: it is designed to be exhaustive, and forgetting to diff a new field silently breaks the Settings UI. That contract is enforced by nobody - no test asserts every AppConfig field has a corresponding branch, so the failure mode is a silently-dropped Settings UI edit for any newly-added config field, invisible to swiftlint or the compiler.
findings.fix: Not a split job - splitting the comparator would only obscure coverage. Add a characterization test that mutates one field at a time in a fixture AppConfig and asserts diff returns exactly one change per field, so a new field added without a matching branch fails the test instead of failing silently in production.
findings.cetico_evidence: SettingsViewModel.diff (:107) has no test at all (no SettingsViewModel reference in Tests). Its own doc comment's exhaustiveness contract is not enforced.
